claims.text: With the seatpost fully extended at the desired ride height, route the hose to the handlebar remote location.
Hold the hose and turn the handlebar side to side; the proper hose length should create a gentle bend and allow the handlebar to turn side to side.
Ensure there are no sharp bends in the hydraulic hose, as a sharp bend will prevent fluid flow.
Ensure there is no tension at the remote when the bar is turned, as too much tension will cause the hose to disconnect from the remote.
Mark the cut location and cut the hydraulic hose using only a hydraulic hose cutter to ensure a square cut and prevent hose damage.

Thread the remote lever hose barb into the hydraulic hose by holding the hose end and rotating the remote lever clockwise while pushing the barb into the hose, stopping when the hose is hand tight on the barb.
Do not over-tighten and strip the threads inside the hydraulic hose; over- or under-tightening can cause hydraulic fluid leaks.
The hydraulic remote system must be bled after a new hose is installed.

claims.text: With the seatpost fully extended and at the desired ride height in the frame, route the hose to the handlebar remote location.
Hold the hose and turn the handlebar side to side; the proper hose length should create a gentle bend and allow the handlebar to turn side to side.
Ensure there are no sharp bends in the hydraulic hose, as a sharp bend will prevent fluid from flowing.
Ensure there is no tension at the remote when the bar is turned, as too much tension will cause the hose to disconnect from the remote.
Mark the cut location and cut the hydraulic hose using only a hydraulic hose cutter to ensure a square cut and prevent damage to the hose.

Thread the remote lever hose barb into the hydraulic hose by holding the end of the hose and rotating the remote lever clockwise while pushing the remote lever barb into the hose; stop when the hose is hand tight on the hose barb.
Do not over-tighten and strip the threads inside the hydraulic hose; if the hose is over or under tightened, hydraulic fluid can leak.
The hydraulic remote system must be bled after a new hose is installed.
The Reverb 1x Remote upgrade lever does not contain hydraulic fluid, and the hydraulic remote system must be bled after a new Reverb 1x Remote lever is installed for the first time.

claims.text: With the seatpost fully extended at the desired ride height, route the hose to the handlebar remote location.
Hold the hose and turn the handlebar side to side; the proper hose length should create a gentle bend and allow the handlebar to turn side to side.
Ensure there are no sharp bends in the hydraulic hose, as a sharp bend prevents fluid flow.
Ensure there is no tension at the remote when the bar is turned, as too much tension will cause the hose to disconnect from the remote.
Mark the cut location and cut the hydraulic hose.
Use only a hydraulic hose cutter to ensure a square cut and prevent damage to the hose.

Thread the remote lever hose barb into the hydraulic hose by holding the end of the hose and rotating the remote lever clockwise while pushing the barb into the hose, stopping when the hose is hand tight on the barb.
Do not over-tighten and strip the threads inside the hydraulic hose; over- or under-tightening can cause hydraulic fluid to leak.
The hydraulic remote system must be bled after a new hose is installed.

claims.text: With the seatpost fully extended and at the desired ride height in the frame, route the hose to the handlebar remote location.
Hold the hose and turn the handlebar side to side; the proper hose length should create a gentle bend and allow the handlebar to turn side to side.
Ensure there are no sharp bends in the hydraulic hose, as a sharp bend will prevent fluid from flowing.
Ensure there is no tension at the remote when the bar is turned, as too much tension will cause the hose to disconnect from the remote.
Mark the cut location and cut the hydraulic hose using only a hydraulic hose cutter to ensure a square cut and prevent damage to the hose.

Thread the remote lever hose barb into the hydraulic hose by holding the end of the hose and rotating the remote lever clockwise while pushing the remote lever barb into the hose; stop when the hose is hand tight on the hose barb.
Do not over-tighten and strip the threads inside the hydraulic hose; if the hose is over or under tightened, hydraulic fluid can leak.
The hydraulic remote system must be bled after a new hose is installed; proceed to Remote System Bleed.

For the Reverb 1x Remote Upgrade Kit, the 1x Remote upgrade lever does not contain hydraulic fluid and the hydraulic remote system must be bled after a new 1x Remote lever is installed for the first time.

steps.text: Only use original MAGURA brake pads. The brake pads must be undamaged and free of grease/oil. The brake pad locking screw must be fitted with fresh threadlock (medium-strength).

warnings.text: Only use original MAGURA brake pads; pads must be undamaged and free of grease/oil.

citation.title: MAGURA GUSTAV PRO Owner's Manual

steps.text: Remove the wheel from your bicycle.

citation.title: MAGURA GUSTAV PRO Owner's Manual

steps.text: Carefully push the brake pads apart as far as they will go using the MAGURA transport device or a wide, grease-free screwdriver.

citation.title: MAGURA GUSTAV PRO Owner's Manual

steps.text: When all brake pistons are in the outermost position, unscrew the brake pad locking screw by turning it anti-clockwise using a Torx T25 spanner.

citation.title: MAGURA GUSTAV PRO Owner's Manual

steps.text: Remove the brake pads from the brake calliper one by one from above.

citation.title: MAGURA GUSTAV PRO Owner's Manual

steps.text: Clean the inside of the brake calliper (small brush, cloth, compressed air, etc.) with a suitable brake cleaner.

citation.title: MAGURA GUSTAV PRO Owner's Manual

steps.text: Insert the new brake pads into the brake calliper from above with the pad carrier plate facing the brake piston.

citation.title: MAGURA GUSTAV PRO Owner's Manual

steps.text: Guide the brake pad locking screw through the brake calliper and the eyelets of the brake pads. The brake pads must sit securely in the brake calliper; check this by pulling on the pad carrier plate.

citation.title: MAGURA GUSTAV PRO Owner's Manual

steps.text: Tighten the brake pad locking screw using a Torx T25 spanner until a tightening torque of 2.5 Nm (22.1 lbf in) is reached.

claims.text: The brake calliper is aligned by applying and holding the brake lever, slightly tightening the retaining screws, and verifying the rotor runs through the centre of the calliper without contact or noise.
The retaining screws are tightened alternately and in stages to 6 Nm (53.1 lbf in).
If the rotor does not run freely or the calliper position is incorrect, loosen the retaining screws and repeat the alignment steps.
The entire surface of the brake pad must be in contact with the friction ring.
After correct alignment and firm tightening, apply the brake lever several times and hold it firmly; no oil should escape and the pressure point must be clearly felt and not change.

claims.text: With the seatpost fully extended at the desired ride height, route the hose to the handlebar remote location and check hose length by turning the handlebar side to side; the proper length creates a gentle bend and allows full handlebar movement.
Avoid sharp bends in the hydraulic hose, which prevent fluid flow, and avoid tension at the remote when the bar is turned, which can cause the hose to disconnect from the remote.
Mark the cut location and cut the hydraulic hose using only a hydraulic hose cutter to ensure a square cut and prevent hose damage.
Thread the remote lever hose barb into the hydraulic hose by holding the hose end and rotating the remote lever clockwise while pushing the barb into the hose, stopping when hand tight.
Do not over-tighten and strip the threads inside the hydraulic hose; over- or under-tightening can cause hydraulic fluid to leak.
The hydraulic remote system must be bled after a new hose is installed; proceed to Remote System Bleed.
For the Reverb 1x Remote Upgrade Kit, the upgrade lever does not contain hydraulic fluid and the system must be bled after the new lever is installed for the first time.

claims.text: The Reverb 1x Remote bleed procedure requires setting the speed adjuster to the full slow position before bleeding.
The Reverb 1x Remote bleed uses a Bleeding Edge syringe bleed tool.
The bleed port screw on the Reverb 1x Remote must be opened by turning it counter-clockwise one quarter turn, then clockwise until light resistance is felt.
The Bleeding Edge syringe bleed tool is inserted into the remote bleed port and turned 1/4 to 1 full turn counter-clockwise to open the bleed system.
After bleeding, the boot must be reinstalled onto the Reverb 1x Remote lever.

The hydraulic remote system must be bled after a new hose is installed; proceed to Remote System Bleed.

claims.text: The hose sizing procedure begins with the seatpost fully extended at the desired ride height, routing the hose to the handlebar remote location.

There should be no tension at the remote when the bar is turned; too much tension will cause the hose to disconnect from the remote.

A notice states to use only a hydraulic hose cutter to ensure a square cut and prevent damage to the hose.
The remote lever hose barb is threaded into the hydraulic hose by holding the hose end and rotating the remote lever clockwise while pushing the barb into the hose, stopping when hand tight.
A notice states not to over-tighten and strip the threads inside the hydraulic hose, because over- or under-tightening can cause hydraulic fluid to leak.
The hydraulic remote system must be bled after a new hose is installed.

claims.text: With the seatpost fully extended and at the desired ride height in the frame, route the hose to the handlebar remote location.
Hold the hose and turn the handlebar side to side; the proper hose length should create a gentle bend and allow the handlebar to turn side to side.
Ensure there are no sharp bends in the hydraulic hose, as a sharp bend will prevent fluid from flowing.
Ensure there is no tension at the remote when the bar is turned, as too much tension will cause the hose to disconnect from the remote.
Mark the cut location and cut the hydraulic hose using only a hydraulic hose cutter to ensure a square cut and prevent hose damage.

Thread the remote lever hose barb into the hydraulic hose by holding the end of the hose and rotating the remote lever clockwise while pushing the remote lever barb into the hose; stop when the hose is hand tight on the hose barb.
Do not over-tighten and strip the threads inside the hydraulic hose; if the hose is over or under tightened, hydraulic fluid can leak.
The hydraulic remote system must be bled after a new hose is installed; proceed to Remote System Bleed.
The Reverb 1x Remote upgrade lever does not contain hydraulic fluid and the hydraulic remote system must be bled after a new Reverb 1x Remote lever is installed for the first time.

claims.text: With the seatpost fully extended at the desired ride height, route the hose to the handlebar remote location.
Hold the hose and turn the handlebar side to side; the proper hose length should create a gentle bend and allow the handlebar to turn side to side.
Ensure there are no sharp bends in the hydraulic hose, as a sharp bend will prevent fluid flow.
Ensure there is no tension at the remote when the bar is turned; too much tension will cause the hose to disconnect from the remote.
Mark the cut location and cut the hydraulic hose using only a hydraulic hose cutter to ensure a square cut and prevent hose damage.

Thread the remote lever hose barb into the hydraulic hose by holding the end of the hose and rotating the remote lever clockwise while pushing the remote lever barb into the hose; stop when the hose is hand tight on the hose barb.
Do not over-tighten and strip the threads inside the hydraulic hose; if the hose is over or under tightened, hydraulic fluid can leak.
The hydraulic remote system must be bled after a new hose is installed; proceed to Remote System Bleed.

For the Reverb 1x Remote Upgrade Kit, the upgrade lever does not contain hydraulic fluid and the hydraulic remote system must be bled after a new Reverb 1x Remote lever is installed for the first time.

The hydraulic remote system must be bled after a new hose is installed; proceed to Remote System Bleed.

For the Reverb 1x Remote Upgrade Kit, the 1x Remote upgrade lever does not contain hydraulic fluid and the hydraulic remote system must be bled after a new 1x Remote lever is installed for the first time; refer to Hose Sizing and Remote Installation - Step 5 for 1x Remote installation.

Do not allow Reverb hydraulic fluid to come into contact with any brake components, as contaminated brake components can compromise brake performance, may cause brake failure, and can lead to serious injury and/or death.

claims.text: Only original MAGURA brake pads may be used, and the brake pads must be undamaged and free of grease/oil.
The brake pad locking screw must be fitted with fresh medium-strength threadlock.
The brake pad locking screw is tightened with a Torx T25 spanner to 2.5 Nm (22.1 lbf in).

New brake pads must be bedded in by slowing from 20 km/h to 5 km/h at least 30 times on a level road, repeating until no further improvement in braking force is noticeable, and bedding in each brake separately.

claims.text: With the seatpost fully extended at the desired ride height, route the hose to the handlebar remote location.
Hold the hose and turn the handlebar side to side; the proper hose length should create a gentle bend and allow the handlebar to turn side to side.
Ensure there are no sharp bends in the hydraulic hose, as a sharp bend will prevent fluid flow.
Ensure there is no tension at the remote when the bar is turned; too much tension will cause the hose to disconnect from the remote.
Mark the cut location and cut the hydraulic hose using only a hydraulic hose cutter to ensure a square cut and prevent hose damage.

Thread the remote lever hose barb into the hydraulic hose by holding the end of the hose and rotating the remote lever clockwise while pushing the remote lever barb into the hose; stop when the hose is hand tight on the hose barb.
Do not over-tighten and strip the threads inside the hydraulic hose; if the hose is over or under tightened, hydraulic fluid can leak.
The hydraulic remote system must be bled after a new hose is installed; proceed to Remote System Bleed.

For the Reverb 1x Remote Upgrade Kit, the upgrade lever does not contain hydraulic fluid and the hydraulic remote system must be bled after a new Reverb 1x Remote lever is installed for the first time.

claims.text: With the seatpost fully extended at the desired ride height in the frame, route the hose to the handlebar remote location.
Hold the hose and turn the handlebar side to side; the proper hose length should create a gentle bend and allow the handlebar to turn side to side.
Ensure there are no sharp bends in the hydraulic hose, because a sharp bend will prevent fluid from flowing.
Ensure there is no tension at the remote when the bar is turned, because too much tension will cause the hose to disconnect from the remote.
Mark the cut location and cut the hydraulic hose.
Use only a hydraulic hose cutter to ensure a square cut and prevent damage to the hose.

Thread the remote lever hose barb into the hydraulic hose by holding the end of the hose and rotating the remote lever clockwise while pushing the remote lever barb into the hose; stop when the hose is hand tight on the hose barb.
Do not over-tighten and strip the threads inside the hydraulic hose; if the hose is over- or under-tightened, hydraulic fluid can leak.
The hydraulic remote system must be bled after a new hose is installed; proceed to Remote System Bleed.

For the Reverb 1x Remote Upgrade Kit, the 1x Remote upgrade lever does not contain hydraulic fluid and the hydraulic remote system must be bled after a new 1x Remote lever is installed for the first time; refer to Hose Sizing and Remote Installation - Step 5 for 1x Remote installation.

Do not allow Reverb hydraulic fluid to come into contact with any brake components, because contaminated brake components can compromise brake performance, may cause brake failure, and can lead to serious injury and/or death.

claims.text: The service steps provided are for lower leg installation on a RockShox Reba suspension fork, specifically hollow bottom fork legs.
Suspension oil should be injected or poured into each lower leg from the dust seal side while holding the lower leg assembly horizontally.
The lower leg assembly should be slid onto the horizontally positioned upper tube assembly until it stops and the spring and damper shafts are visible through the shaft bolt holes.
Shaft bolts should be inserted into the threaded shaft ends through the lower leg shaft holes and tightened to 7.3 N·m (65 in-lb) with a 5 mm hex or 10 mm socket wrench.
For hollow bottom fork legs, a socket extension is needed for the 5 mm bolt and a deep 10 mm socket is needed for the Dual Air shaft nut.
For forks with an external rebound adjuster, the external rebound damper knob should be inserted into the rebound damper shaft bolt and pushed in until secure.
Air sprung forks should be inflated to the appropriate pressure per the air chart, and the positive and negative air valve caps should be threaded onto the air valves.
The entire fork should be sprayed with isopropyl alcohol and wiped with a clean rag.

citation.title: MAGURA GUSTAV PRO Owner's Manual

steps.text: Remove the wheel from your bicycle.

citation.title: MAGURA GUSTAV PRO Owner's Manual

citation.title: MAGURA GUSTAV PRO Owner's Manual

steps.text: When all brake pistons are in the outermost position, unscrew the brake pad locking screw by turning it anti-clockwise using a Torx T25 spanner.

steps.text: Remove the brake pads from the brake calliper one by one from above.

Step 2: Hold the hose and turn the handlebar side to side. The proper length of the hose should create a gentle bend and allow the handlebar to turn side to side.
Step 3: Mark the cut location.
Step 4: Cut the hydraulic hose.

Step 5: Thread the remote lever hose barb into the hydraulic hose. Hold the end of the hose and rotate the remote lever clockwise while pushing the remote lever barb into the hose. Stop when the hose is hand tight on the hose barb.

Notice: Ensure there are no sharp bends in the hydraulic hose. A sharp bend in the hose will prevent fluid from flowing. Ensure there is no tension at the remote when the bar is turned. Too much tension will cause the hose to disconnect from the remote.
Notice: To ensure a square cut and to prevent damage to the hose, use only a hydraulic hose cutter.
Notice: Do not over-tighten and strip the threads inside the hydraulic hose. If the hose is over or under tightened, hydraulic fluid can leak.

claims.text: Step 1: With the seatpost fully extended and at the desired ride height in the frame, route the hose to the handlebar remote location.
Step 2: Hold the hose and turn the handlebar side to side. The proper length of the hose should create a gentle bend and allow the handlebar to turn side to side.
Step 3: Mark the cut location.
Step 4: Cut the hydraulic hose.

Step 5: Thread the remote lever hose barb into the hydraulic hose. Hold the end of the hose and rotate the remote lever clockwise while pushing the remote lever barb into the hose. Stop when the hose is hand tight on the hose barb.

Notice: Ensure there are no sharp bends in the hydraulic hose. A sharp bend in the hose will prevent fluid from flowing. Ensure there is no tension at the remote when the bar is turned. Too much tension will cause the hose to disconnect from the remote.
Notice: To ensure a square cut and to prevent damage to the hose, use only a hydraulic hose cutter.
Notice: Do not over-tighten and strip the threads inside the hydraulic hose. If the hose is over or under tightened, hydraulic fluid can leak.

claims.text: Step 1: With the seatpost fully extended and at the desired ride height in the frame, route the hose to the handlebar remote location.
Step 2: Hold the hose and turn the handlebar side to side. The proper length of the hose should create a gentle bend and allow the handlebar to turn side to side.
Step 3: Mark the cut location.
Step 4: Cut the hydraulic hose.

Step 5: Thread the remote lever hose barb into the hydraulic hose. Hold the end of the hose and rotate the remote lever clockwise while pushing the remote lever barb into the hose. Stop when the hose is hand tight on the hose barb.

Notice: Ensure there are no sharp bends in the hydraulic hose. A sharp bend in the hose will prevent fluid from flowing. Ensure there is no tension at the remote when the bar is turned. Too much tension will cause the hose to disconnect from the remote.
Notice: To ensure a square cut and to prevent damage to the hose, use only a hydraulic hose cutter.
Notice: Do not over-tighten and strip the threads inside the hydraulic hose. If the hose is over or under tightened, hydraulic fluid can leak.

claims.text: Step 1: With the seatpost fully extended and at the desired ride height in the frame, route the hose to the handlebar remote location.
Step 2: Hold the hose and turn the handlebar side to side. The proper length of the hose should create a gentle bend and allow the handlebar to turn side to side.
Step 3: Mark the cut location.
Step 4: Cut the hydraulic hose.

Step 5: Thread the remote lever hose barb into the hydraulic hose. Hold the end of the hose and rotate the remote lever clockwise while pushing the remote lever barb into the hose. Stop when the hose is hand tight on the hose barb.

Notice: Ensure there are no sharp bends in the hydraulic hose. A sharp bend in the hose will prevent fluid from flowing. Ensure there is no tension at the remote when the bar is turned. Too much tension will cause the hose to disconnect from the remote.
Notice: To ensure a square cut and to prevent damage to the hose, use only a hydraulic hose cutter.
Notice: Do not over-tighten and strip the threads inside the hydraulic hose. If the hose is over or under tightened, hydraulic fluid can leak.
